lines.text: How did a colossal three-hundred-foot copper statue built in Paris cross the stormy Atlantic Ocean to New York Harbor?
It arrived as the world's most epic jigsaw puzzle.
Designed by sculptor Bartholdi with an internal iron skeleton engineered by Gustave Eiffel, it was fully assembled in Paris first.
To transport it, workers painstakingly disassembled Lady Liberty into three hundred and fifty individual pieces.
The crates were loaded aboard a French navy steamship that nearly capsized in heavy oceanic gales.
When it reached New York in eighteen eighty-five, Americans reassembled the pieces around an iron truss skeleton over four months.
Originally shiny reddish bronze, copper oxidation turned her into the iconic green monument we cherish today.
